table_title: List the top 3 food sources for each major vitamin with approximate content and source type.
db_analog: SELECT vitamin, list_position, food, approximate_content, source_type FROM vitamin_food_sources WHERE vitamin IN ('Vitamin A','Vitamin B12','Vitamin C','Vitamin D','Vitamin E','Vitamin K') ORDER BY vitamin, list_position
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-vitamin articles accessed 2026-04-29. The 6-vitamin universe (Vitamin A, B12, C, D, E, K) is anchored to Wikipedia 'Vitamin' article which classifies all 6 as essential vitamins (the article lists 13 in total: 4 fat-soluble — A, D, E, K — and 9 water-soluble — 8 B vitamins and Vitamin C; the staged 6 are picked to span both classification groups). Per-vitamin food source listings + content + source type are anchored to each per-vitamin Wikipedia article's Sources / Dietary Sources section. Vitamin C / E / A use mg or μg per 100 g (the per-vitamin article tables); Vitamin K uses mixed per-100g (K2 sources: Nattō, Egg yolk) and per-serving (K1 sources: Collard greens 1/2 cup, Spinach 1/2 cup, Kale 1 cup) because the article's K1 leafy-green table reports per-cup or per-half-cup; Vitamin D uses IU per serving (3 oz fish or 1/2 cup mushrooms or 1 cup milk) per the article's reporting convention; Vitamin B12 uses qualitative descriptors because the Vitamin B12 Wikipedia article does not provide a numeric food-content table — the 5 staged B12 rows preserve the article's verbatim food-name list (organ meats from lamb, beef, turkey + crab meat + fortified breakfast cereals) with a 'qualitative' tag. Schema follows the cycles 1+2+3 lessons from prior scaled_enumeration instances: selection-not-ranked framing in table_title; composite PK (Vitamin, Food) with List Position as a non-key numeric display ordinal; per-row Wikipedia article cited from cycle 0 (each row is cited via its vitamin's article).
_extraction_notes: Derived from vitamins_top5_food_sources by deterministic filter/projection on the parent CSV. List Position filter <= 3.
